description: Agent Support Operations: submit escalation records with the escalation triggers they answer to: each trigger with its id, reference, the condition that calls for escalation, the wait in hours within which the escalation must be raised and who it goes to; each support ticket with its id, reference, the trigger it met, the moment the record shows the trigger met and the moment the customer left the conversation; each escalation record with its id, reference, the support ticket, the moment raised and who raised it, the moment acted on, the moment closed, who closed it and who reviewed it before the close. The signed report gives the triggers, the tickets and the escalations, each ticket that met a trigger against the escalations recorded for it, each escalation against the action taken on it, each closed escalation’s closing hand against the hand that raised it and a second review, and each escalation’s raising against the moment the customer left, and counts them, and names divergent escalation records: a trigger met with no escalation recorded, an escalation recorded and never acted on, an escalation closed by the same hand that raised it with no second review, and an escalation raised only after the customer had already left; then an escalation raised later than its trigger’s wait and an escalation naming a ticket the record does not hold, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No triggers, no tickets, no escalations, or a ticket naming a trigger the record does not state leaves those points unverified. Tickets, triggers and escalations match by letters and digits and hands without case or punctuation, and waits count in hours between two moments that carry a time. This reads whether each escalation the triggers call for is raised, acted on, reviewed and raised in time. Verdict support_escalation_divergent, support_escalation_partial, support_escalation_unverified or support_escalation_consistent. POST /api/support-escalation-check. Reads the support records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it answers no customer, sends no message and opens, closes or changes no ticket, which stay with the support team, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Support Operations reads support operation records: ticket logs, first response records, resolution records, escalation records, promise records, performance records, backlog records and the support summary, each against the queue record, the stated response commitments, the customer confirmations, the stated escalation triggers, what the records show happened, the stated service commitments, the ticket list or the records beneath it. The family’s ground is support work already done, read across the whole queue: the DiligenceOps support brief reads one support conversation and lists the promises made in it, and the Agent Feedback family reads the loop around feedback on work, while this family checks whether the support operation’s records hold together across tickets. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-support-operations-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-support-operations/.

acted_at.description: When the escalation was acted on, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

closed_at.description: When the escalation was closed, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

closed_by.description: Who closed it, as the record names them.

raised_at.description: When the escalation was raised, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

raised_by.description: Who raised it, as the record names them.

reviewed_by.description: Who reviewed it before close, as the record names them.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

tickets.description: Each support ticket the triggers cover.

customer_left_at.description: When the customer left or abandoned the conversation, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

met_at.description: When the record shows the trigger met, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

trigger.description: The trigger the ticket met reference.

condition.description: The condition that calls for escalation.

wait_hours.description: How long after the trigger is met the escalation must be raised, in hours.

name: wever_support-escalation-check
title: Support escalation check
